newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--SING TAO -- Former Bar Council chairman Gladys Li said the provisional legislature violated the Basic Law, Hong Kong's post-handover constitution, and argued the Court of Appeals had the power to handle legal challenges against the interim body.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- A seminar attended by experts from both China and Hong Kong discussed the possibility of linking Hong Kong and major cities in nearby Guangdong province by railway.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Seventy-five former senior government officials have set up a consultancy company to provide services to private businesses in dealing with the government.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Secretary for Civil Service W.K. Lam is planning to change the present annual salary review system, because this year's salary increase was not well accepted by civil servants' groups.

-- MING PAO -- Six foreigners were detained in Beijing for selling 54 kilograms of "ecstacy" pills in a hotel. The expatriates confessed that they had bought the pills in southern China and planned to sell them for about HK$300 each.

-- Three peasants from China's Hunan province were recently caught with forged Renminbi notes worth about HK$1.5 million. They had bought the fake notes in Guangdong province and were caught on a train while on their way to sell them in the north.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The government proposed a return to corporate voting to decide who participates in polls for nine new functional constituencies, instead of individual voting used in the 1995 legislative election.
